title: RE J. Lance Acree v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because Acree lacked standing under BCO 43-1.
first_summary: RE Acree attempted to complain directly to Tennessee Valley Presbytery about action taken at a meeting where he was not a commissioner. The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because BCO 43-1 gave him no standing to complain against that action. It added that Presbytery should itself have declined to adjudicate the complaint.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The decision is Case 2021-07, dated March 3, 2022, in the 49th Assembly minutes; the SJC vote was 23-0-0.
evidence_notes.dispute: Acree filed a BCO 43-1 complaint with Presbytery concerning action at a meeting where he was not a ruling-elder commissioner.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The officers recommended administrative out-of-order status and inability to cure; the SJC ruled Acree lacked standing and said Presbytery should have declined to adjudicate.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The ruling is procedural and does not decide the merits of the challenged Presbytery action.
